Annotate features from spectral library match results

Source: R/method_annotate_PeakAnnotationLibraryMatch.R
annotateLibMatch-PeakAnnotationFromLibraryMatch-method.Rd

Two-phase annotation dispatched on a PeakAnnotationFromLibraryMatch-class object.

Phase 1 — annotate_librarymatch_phase1_cpp():

  • Runs Check_Iso_Charge once on the union of all library-matched features and the full pool. Produces a global isotope label table shared by both phases — isotope is never re-computed.

  • For each library-match group: adduct match (Tier 1a), isotope lookup (Tier 1b), pairwise NL within group (Tier 1c), precursor/MS2 match (Tier 1d), unexplained (Tier 2).

  • RT is used automatically when available; if RT values are NA the RT gate simply does not fire.

  • Returns annotated rows plus confirmed_M (confirmed neutral masses with reference RT) and iso_labels (global isotope table) for Phase 2.

Phase 2 — annotate_librarymatch_phase2_cpp() (only when FT slot is non-empty):

  • For each confirmed M from Phase 1, scans pool features not already annotated within rt_exp_threshold s of the compound reference RT and ppm_exp ppm of any adduct mass (Tier 1a_exp).

  • Looks up iso labels from the Phase 1 global table (Tier 1b_exp).

  • Runs pairwise NL within the same-M expansion group (Tier 1c_exp).

Usage

# S4 method for class 'PeakAnnotationFromLibraryMatch'
annotateLibMatch(object, cutoff_MH = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

A PeakAnnotationFromLibraryMatch-class object.

cutoff_MH

logical. If TRUE, adds a cutoff_to_MH column to the result that classifies each Tier2_Unexplained feature as "above_MH" or "below_MH" relative to the theoretical \([M+H]^+\) / \([M-H]^-\) ion of the matched compound. All other tiers and rows with unknown Compound_M receive NA. Default FALSE — the column is not added unless explicitly requested.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A data.frame with columns: feature_name, mz, rt, intensity, Compound_name, Lib_group, Ion_type, Compound_M, PI_match, grp_anno_match, grp_anno_ppm, grp_anno_mda, grp_anno_confidence, exp_anno_match, exp_anno_ppm, exp_anno_mda, exp_anno_confidence, NL_match, iso_annotation, reference_tier, annotation_phase, Match_peak_score, inner_cosine, outer_cosine. When cutoff_MH = TRUE, the additional column cutoff_to_MH is appended (see cutoff_MH parameter above).
